name: Weak-coupling phase sparsification for toy Module-LWE QAOA
cohort: All 64 previously inspected toy Module-LWE development examples; exploratory, not a fresh final holdout
hypothesis: Deleting the weakest 25 percent of nonzero ZZ interactions retains at least 95 percent of aggregate exact optimum sampling performance while reducing mean compiled all-to-all CX count by at least 20 percent.
primary_quality_checks: ratio of mean per-shot optimum probability >= 0.95
ratio of mean exact solved fraction at 1024 shots >= 0.95
secondary_comparators: full per-instance tuned QAOA from EXP-003
random removal of 25 percent of interactions across 5 seeds
rule: Remove floor(fraction * number of nonzero upper-triangular J entries), smallest absolute J first, lexicographic tie order. Keep all single-qubit fields, original normalization, mixer, initial state, box, and original decoding objective unchanged.
angle_policies: reuse frozen EXP-003 global angles without retraining
retrain one global angle pair per sparsity on the same 16 separate public training instances, minimizing ORIGINAL expected energy

compilation.topology: all-to-all, not a physical IBM device

limitations: One toy parameter set and one QAOA layer; all 64 examples are already inspected development data.
Magnitude pruning is inspired by sparsified-phase QAOA literature, not a reproduction of a ground-state-preserving construction. No optimum-preservation guarantee.
The scored objective and candidate box remain unchanged, but the quantum phase operator is approximated.
All-to-all compiled CX count excludes physical-device routing, durations, calibration, and noise. No hardware or quantum advantage claim.
Aggregate retention can conceal losses on individual instances; paired distributions and worst cases are reported.
Separate global retraining costs are recorded; the primary candidate uses unchanged angles and no retraining.
Bootstrap intervals describe this development cohort under instance resampling and are not confirmatory population claims.
